sources.title: Summer hours and tickets (Sunshine Village gondola and Standish chair)
sources.note: 2026 summer operations: opened in the first week of July, closed on the third Sunday of September; gondola 8:00 to 18:00.

sources.title: Banff Sunshine Village announces summer opening for 2025 season
sources.note: 2025 summer season: opened on the last Friday of June, closed on the third Sunday of September.

sources.title: Weather, Banff National Park (monthly averages)
sources.note: Averages without stated years. Banff, September: high 16.1, low 2.7 C. Lake Louise, September: high 14.3, low -0.8 C; June: high 17.2, low 2.1 C. Banff, August: high 21.6 C.

sources.title: Canadian Climate Normals 1991-2020, BANFF CS (3050519)
sources.note: Precipitation, June: 73.3 mm (the wettest month); September: 44.9 mm. Days with 1 mm or more, June: 11.3; July: 8.2; August: 8.3; September: 7.9. Snowfall, June: 1.7 cm; September: 7.9 cm.

sources.title: Alberta Tourism Market Monitor, December 2019 (national park attendance by month, source Parks Canada)
sources.note: Independent visitors, thousands, 2019. Banff: Jun 389.1, Jul 688.5, Aug 723.8, Sep 472.3. Jasper: Jun 237.9, Jul 468.4, Aug 495.7, Sep 319.8. Monthly only; no weekly split.

sources.title: Alberta general holidays
sources.note: Canada Day: the first of July, or the second when the first is a Sunday. Labour Day dates listed for 2026 and 2027 are both the first Monday of September.

sources.title: Calgary Board of Education school calendar 2025-26 (Belfast School)
sources.note: First day of classes the Tuesday after Labour Day; last day of school the last Friday of June (system-wide early dismissal). One school's copy of the board calendar.

sources.title: Hiking, Banff National Park
sources.note: Prime hiking season July through mid-September; until late June many passes snow-bound with avalanche hazard; most alpine passes snow-free by mid-July; Healy Pass larches turn in late September.

sources.title: Elk safety, Jasper National Park
sources.note: Calving season mid-May to the end of June; rutting season the start of September to mid-October; keep at least 30 m from all elk.

sources.title: Day visits (canoe dock)
sources.note: Due to water levels the canoe dock runs only from mid-June to mid-September; first come, first served.

sources.title: Where to find golden larch trees in the Canadian Rockies
sources.note: Best time between mid-September and early October, varying with the weather. Promotional page; no page date.

windows.label: Second week of September
windows.best_for: The plan as written: after the long weekend, with the first larch colour late in the trip

crowd.note: Banff had 472 thousand visits in September against 724 thousand in August; that the weeks after Labour Day are the quieter part of September is our inference.

plus.text: Starts after the Labour Day long weekend, once schools are back
Larch colour season starts around mid-September, inside the trip's second week
Sunshine Meadows gondola still runs on plan day 2; it closes later in September
Fewer wet days than June: about 8 days a month with 1 mm of rain or more at Banff

minus.text: Cold nights: Lake Louise's September average low is just below freezing
Snow is possible up high: Banff averages about 8 cm of snowfall in September
Moraine Lake's canoe dock runs only to mid-September, so it can be closed by plan day 11
Elk rut season: keep at least 30 m from elk around the townsites

events.rule: Labour Day is the first Monday of September; this window always starts after that long weekend
